question_text: A 21-year-old college student is admitted to the emergency department with complaints of pharyngitis, headache, and a persistent, non-productive, dry, hacking cough. The patient complains of feeling tired and fatigued and denies fever/chills. On physical examination, her mucosa is pale. A complete blood count is remarkable for decreased hemoglobin. A direct Coombs test comes back positive. Which of the following statements is true regarding the complications associated with Mycoplasma pneumoniae?

                    ### Question
                    A 21-year-old college student is admitted to the emergency department with complaints of pharyngitis, headache, and a persistent, non-productive, dry, hacking cough. The patient complains of feeling tired and fatigued and denies fever/chills. On physical examination, her mucosa is pale. A complete blood count is remarkable for decreased hemoglobin. The physician suspects viral pneumonia, but the sputum culture tests come back with the following description: ‘fried-egg shaped colonies on sterol-containing media, and mulberry-shaped colonies on media containing sterols’. A direct Coombs test comes back positive. Which of the following statements is true regarding the complications associated with Mycoplasma pneumoniae?

                    ### Options

opb. It is similarly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus
opc. Red blood cells bind to IgG in warm temperatures > 37°C (98.6°F)
opd. Red blood cells bind to IgM in cold temperatures < 37°C (98.6°F)
ope. The underlying mechanism is complement-independent.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection can lead to autoimmune hemolytic anemia, as evidenced by a positive direct Coombs test. This condition involves red blood cells binding to IgG in warm temperatures (> 37°C/98.6°F), indicating a warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. The underlying mechanism is complement-independent.
